name: Quiet Hours
brand_voice: A close third-person narrator telling small, complete stories about ordinary people at a turning point — a shift ending, a debt coming due, a conversation that has been postponed for years. Restrained, specific, no moral at the end.
hook_format: She had rehearsed the sentence for six years. She had ninety seconds to say it.

pain_points: short-form content that never resolves anything
wanting a complete story in one sitting
melodrama that tells you how to feel
content_triggers: one decision that cannot be taken back
two people and one unsaid thing
an ordinary job seen from the inside
engagement_drivers: tell us what you would have said

_image_style_note: Leads with an observable, not with 'cinematic'. The anti-slop linter (omnicast/storyboard/slop.py) blocks empty evaluators in the opening clause: 'cinematic' names no camera, no light and no lens, so it spends the most heavily weighted clause in the prompt on an average of everything that word has ever labelled.
image_style_prompt: 16mm film grain, soft directional light from one window, shallow depth of field, desaturated restrained palette, unretouched naturalistic faces
image_style_negative: cgi, 3d render, plastic skin, over-saturated, hdr, beauty retouching, watermark, text, logo, extra limbs, deformed hands, collage, split panel
image_style_lock: as a single cinematic photograph with consistent film stock and lighting across the whole video
_storyboard_note: This channel is the one that exercises omnicast.storyboard. Character consistency here means faces: a cast is extracted from the script, each member gets a multi-view reference sheet, and every frame binds its references by token. Approval is deliberately manual — a wrong reference image is wrong in every frame that attaches it, so a human confirms the cast once and the rest of the board runs unattended.
